title: Sinus Bradycardia: EKG Characteristics, Causes and Treatment

notes.text: Sinus bradycardia
A concise, newly authored revision guide for this topic. Use the video for the instructor’s full explanation; these notes do not claim to transcribe it.
Sinus bradycardia has a sinus P wave before each QRS with a slower-than-expected heart rate.
Athletic conditioning and sleep can produce physiologic slowing.
Hypoperfusion rather than the heart-rate number alone determines urgent clinical significance.
Medication effects and metabolic abnormalities are potentially reversible causes.

title: Premature Ventricular Contractions (PVCs): EKG Characteristics, Causes and Treatment

notes.text: Ventricular ectopy
A concise, newly authored revision guide for this topic. Use the video for the instructor’s full explanation; these notes do not claim to transcribe it.
Premature ventricular contractions originate in ventricular tissue before the next expected sinus beat.
Wide QRS complexes are typical because activation does not follow the usual ventricular conduction sequence.
Compensatory pauses often follow premature ventricular beats.
Structural heart disease and symptom burden influence evaluation.

title: Rapid Sequence Intubation (RSI): Airway Risk Assessment, Technique, Induction and Paralytic Agents

notes.text: Rapid sequence intubation concepts
A concise, newly authored revision guide for this topic. Use the video for the instructor’s full explanation; these notes do not claim to transcribe it.
Preoxygenation increases the oxygen reserve before induction and apnea.
Neuromuscular blockade facilitates intubation but does not provide sedation or analgesia.
Waveform capnography is used to help confirm tracheal tube placement and monitor ventilation.
Rescue oxygenation planning is essential before attempting a difficult airway.

title: Premature Atrial Contraction (PACs): ECG Characteristics, Causes, Diagnosis and Treatment

notes.text: Atrial ectopy
A concise, newly authored revision guide for this topic. Use the video for the instructor’s full explanation; these notes do not claim to transcribe it.
Premature atrial contractions arise from an atrial focus outside the sinus node.
Abnormal P-wave morphology can distinguish an ectopic atrial beat from a sinus beat.
Narrow QRS complexes are usual unless there is aberrant ventricular conduction.
Blocked atrial beats occur when a premature impulse reaches a refractory AV node.

title: Extraglottic Airway: Supraglottic and Retroglottic Devices, Advantages and Disadvantages

notes.text: Extraglottic airway devices
A concise, newly authored revision guide for this topic. Use the video for the instructor’s full explanation; these notes do not claim to transcribe it.
Supraglottic devices establish a ventilatory pathway above the vocal cords.
Rescue ventilation is an important role when mask ventilation or tracheal intubation is difficult.
Aspiration protection is less complete than with a correctly positioned cuffed tracheal tube.
Device position and an adequate seal are essential to effective ventilation.

title: Spine Motion Restriction: Indications, Equipment, Steps to Do it and Contraindications

notes.text: Spinal motion restriction
A concise, newly authored revision guide for this topic. Use the video for the instructor’s full explanation; these notes do not claim to transcribe it.
Motion restriction aims to limit additional movement when spinal injury is suspected.
Neurologic examination documents motor and sensory function before and after movement when possible.
Clinical assessment guides selection of patients who need spinal precautions.
Prolonged immobilization can cause pressure injury and respiratory discomfort.

title: Sinus Arrhythmia: ECG Characteristics, Presentation & Treatment

notes.text: Respiratory sinus arrhythmia
A concise, newly authored revision guide for this topic. Use the video for the instructor’s full explanation; these notes do not claim to transcribe it.
Respiratory sinus arrhythmia is cyclic variation in sinus rate with breathing.
Inspiration commonly increases heart rate while expiration slows it.
Sinus P waves remain present with the expected atrial morphology.
Young healthy people commonly show this benign variation.

notes.text: Bag-mask ventilation concepts
A concise, newly authored revision guide for this topic. Use the video for the instructor’s full explanation; these notes do not claim to transcribe it.
Mask seal is essential to limit leak during assisted ventilation.
Airway positioning improves patency and the delivery of breaths.
Visible chest rise helps assess whether ventilation is reaching the lungs.
Excessive ventilation can increase gastric inflation and impair venous return.

notes.text: Noninvasive positive pressure
A concise, newly authored revision guide for this topic. Use the video for the instructor’s full explanation; these notes do not claim to transcribe it.
CPAP applies a continuous positive airway pressure throughout the respiratory cycle.
Bilevel ventilation provides different inspiratory and expiratory pressures.
Inspiratory pressure support helps reduce work of breathing and improve ventilation.
Inability to protect the airway is an important limitation of noninvasive ventilation.

title: Head Tilt/Chin Lift, Jaw Thrust, Oropharyngeal Airway and Nasopharyngeal Airway

notes.text: Airway assessment and patency
A concise, newly authored revision guide for this topic. Use the video for the instructor’s full explanation; these notes do not claim to transcribe it.
Tongue displacement can obstruct the upper airway in an unconscious person.
Jaw thrust can help open the airway when cervical motion should be minimized.
Oropharyngeal airways are generally used only when the gag reflex is absent.
Oxygenation and ventilation must both be assessed because a patent airway alone does not guarantee adequate gas exchange.
